newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent eases after unsurprising U.S. stocks data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent eases after unsurprising U.S. stocks data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were marginally weaker on Thursday after the release overnight of stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which traders sad were neutral to slightly negative.
July Brent had sunk four cents a barrel to $19.20 by 1133 GMT, after trading in a narrow 10-cent range, while June gas oil was 25 cents a tonne up at $173.25.

"The focus for trade - at least early on - will be the (API) statistics which were neutral to slightly bearish," brokers GNI said in a daily report, adding that the market was likely to test lower numbers.
The API data showed a weekly rise in crude stocks of 1.4 million barrels and a weekly fall in gasoline inventories of 1.1 million barrels
"The APIs show no great surprises," said Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives. "Thus prices are relatively unchanged."
Technical analysts said $19.00 was an important level of support, and below that level a gap on the July chart at $18.80-$18.88 would also provide support.
"We view this area as a pivot point," GNI said.
